text: PM directs ministries to stimulate year-end consumer demand

HÀ NỘI - The Prime Minister has instructed ministries, sectors and local authorities to urgently implement measures to boost consumer demand and develop the domestic market during the final months of 2026 and the 2027 Tết (Lunar New Year) holiday.
The market is expected to remain under pressure in the final months of 2026 and early 2027 from rising costs of imported raw materials and fuels, as well as production, business and credit costs.
These pressures could weigh on consumer purchasing power and slow growth in the domestic market.

Under Directive No. 40/CT-TTg, the Prime Minister has asked the State Bank of Việt Nam (SBV) to continue pursuing a proactive and flexible monetary policy to help curb inflation and support economic growth.

The SBV is also tasked with directing credit institutions to streamline procedures, cut costs and consider reducing lending rates to help businesses expand production, operations and technological innovation.
The PM has also called for banks to develop a diverse range of consumer credit products tailored to meet the legitimate capital needs of individuals for year-end and Lunar New Year shopping.
The expansion of consumer credit must be accompanied by strict credit risk management to ensure the operational safety of the financial system.

Furthermore, the SBV has been instructed to continue promoting cashless payments, facilitating the use of services for purchasing goods, particularly through online channels, by both individuals and businesses.

Under the directive, the Ministry of Finance has been required to manage tax and fee policies in a reasonable manner, with the aim of reducing the cost of living and increasing the spending capacity of households.
To safeguard purchasing power and stabilise the market, the PM has directed relevant authorities to review factors that could drive up prices, particularly for essential goods.
For goods and services subject to state-regulated pricing, any adjustments must follow an appropriate roadmap, with a focus on limiting price increases at this time.

Relevant authorities must ensure a balance between the supply and demand of essential goods; strictly penalise acts of speculation, hoarding, price manipulation, and the exploitation of market fluctuations to impose unreasonable price hikes; and intensify efforts to combat smuggling and commercial fraud.

According to the directive, the Ministry of Industry and Trade (MoIT) will support businesses in developing the domestic market, connecting supply and demand, expanding distribution channels and improving market access

It will also step up trade promotion under the "Vietnamese people prioritise using Vietnamese goods" campaign, strengthen Vietnamese brand recognition and promote domestic consumption, including through the "Vietnamese goods for the Vietnamese people" programme for 2026-2030.

The ministry will work with local authorities and industry associations to organise major promotional events, trade fairs, exhibitions and supply-demand matching programmes, particularly in the year-end and Tết period, to boost sales of domestic products and OCOP goods while linking trade promotion with investment, cultural and tourism activities.
Local authorities will organise Vietnamese goods fairs, promotional campaigns and market linkages, while supporting retail expansion in rural, remote and island areas.
Transport and logistics firms must ensure smooth goods distribution to meet peak demand and prevent shortages. - BIZHUB/VNS
